title: Trumpeter Ned and small uptown bands
summary: Dawson cannot place Ned and mentions small bands around the Garden District.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Trumpeters I admired: rating the horn players

blocks.x: Speaking about those old trumpet players, I wonder, do you remember this man, uh, Ned? You just call him Ned. Ned?

I don't know what his, that's his first name or last name, Ned. Supposed to have been about the time of Buddy Bolden. I don't know, came from uptown I believe, but I don't know. I don't know. Ned. Ned.
I can't, I can't place that. Yeah. Trumpet player.
Yeah. Yeah, that's what I heard. Seems like somebody told me he was a good blues man, but I'm not sure. Look it up.

I ain't never, I've been playing them out a long time, but I can't do it. Yeah, yeah. They had a lot of these fellas, you know, but they didn't do much, you know, they were different bands, big bands, you know, they used to, they had a lot of little skacky bands up around the Garden District up there, up that way. Some over across, over the river too. So you never, we never hear of them down here very seldom, you know. They had a lot of things, they used to call them, they used to have them fish fries on Saturday nights and them fellas would play in the three and four piece job like that with them, you know. And, uh.
